thread:
Maya: fyi GreenStone reporting intermittent 429s in prod since 11:02 UTC. RPM around 980 for their token, TPM ~58k over last 15m. They’re single-tenant. Can someone triage? @samir
Samir: can you paste one of the response headers and a sample request id? also which region?
Maya: region=us-west2. sample request id=req_01F8XYZ
Maya: response headers:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rw-rate-limit-minute: 1000
x-rw-rate-limit-remaining-minute: 0
x-rw-rate-limit-timestamp: 1729003200
x-rw-rate-limit-window: fixed
retry-after: 12
```
Samir: interesting — header shows fixed minute window and zero remaining. rpm 980 < 1000 though; suggests multiple tokens or per-route caps. Did they use multiple concurrent tokens? any proxy in front?
Maya: they use a proxy (api-gateway.company.com) but claim no retries. logs show bursts at top-of-minute aligned with cron jobs.
Ingrid: if bursts align to minute boundaries they hit the fixed window. Our smoothing helps but client change needed. Recommend jittered spread or leaky-bucket client.
Samir: short-term ops move: we can bump their token minute limit to 1500 for 30m while they deploy smoothing. want me to request quota bump?
Maya: yes please. Also can we enable prefix KV caching for their route to reduce token cost for repeated prompts?
Luis: added checklist — enable debug logs, collect sample trace (trace_id=req_01F8XYZ), and replay the pattern to staging with their key.
Deploy-bot: quota bump request filed for account greenstone-prod; pending ops approval.
Ops-bot: snapshot of proxy logs saved to /ops/snapshots/greenstone/1729003333.log
Samir: client guidance I sent to GreenStone:
```
1) add randomized jitter to schedule windows
2) implement exponential backoff with capped retries
3) prefer streaming where possible to reduce per-request tokens
4) check for cross-service duplication of same token
```
Maya: they confirmed they have a cron that runs at :00 every minute with parallel workers — that explains the top-of-minute spike.
Ingrid: long-term: propose either Dedicated capacity (predictable throughput) or route-level smoothing + token grouping.
Luis: next steps: (1) approve 30m quota bump, (2) run replay in staging + verify no duplicate tokens, (3) provide client with sample backoff snippet.
Maya: thanks — I'll coordinate customer patch. :thumbsup:
Samir: bump approved and applied (1500 RPM for 1 hour). monitor and report back in 20m.
Maya: noted, will close when stable.
